subject: Deployment mode selection & migration follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode selection & migration follow-up

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking the time to walk through Nova Healths LLM roadmap earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Recap from the call
- Workloads: mixed generation and embeddings; some low-latency interactive flows and batch inference for reporting.
- Deployment options we discussed: Hosted API (fastest to ship), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool, predictable throughput), Private VPC or on-prem (for strict data residency/PHI).
- Migration sources you mentioned: currently using OpenAI endpoints plus a small in-house Triton cluster for heavy models.

Questions and info we need to size the right pilot
- Are you primarily migrating from OpenAI hosted API, or will you continue to use your Triton cluster in parallel?
- Compliance constraints: do you require VPC only, or will Dedicated with contractual controls and SOC2 evidence work for an initial phase?
- Expected steady state and peak QPS and typical tokens per request.
- Preferred timeline for pilot and procurement steps.

Next steps I propose
1) Technical deep dive with Rishi and Priyom to validate throughput, network, and model support.
2) We'll put together a Dedicated pilot proposal and pricing estimate, plus checklist for VPC/private deployment path.
3) If helpful, we can provision a short Dedicated pilot to compare latency and cost against your current stack.

Would you be available next week for a 60 minute deep-dive? Please reply with a couple of times that work and any network contact we should loop in.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novahealth.com
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode selection & migration follow-up

Hi Marissa,

Great to recap, thanks. A few clarifications from our side that should help with sizing:

Current landscape
- Primary traffic today goes to OpenAI-hosted endpoints for rapid prototyping. We also operate a small Triton cluster for higher-cost models and private datasets.
- Goal is to migrate production traffic off OpenAI over the next 3 months while keeping the Triton cluster for very large model runs initially.

Compliance and constraints
- We handle PHI; long term we need Private VPC or on-prem data plane. For the pilot, Dedicated with contractual assurances and SOC2 evidence is acceptable as long as data egress is controlled.
- Data residency: US only.

Scale and models
- Average QPS: ~30 reqs/s; peak observed burst up to ~120 reqs/s.
- Mix of models: Llama 2 13B for many interactive flows, Llama 2 70B and a couple of closed-source models for higher-quality generation and embeddings.
- Typical tokens per request: 150-600 depending on flow.

Attachments
- Ive attached our infra assessment and a short migration notes doc for your engineers.

Asks
- Can you share a rough estimate for a Dedicated pilot and any change control requirements for moving to a Private VPC later?
- We will loop procurement on pricing and SOW.

Available for a deep-dive next Tue or Wed afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Director of ML Engineering, Nova Health
alex.chen@novahealth.com
Attachment: nova-infra-assessment.pdf

Hi Alex, Marissa,

Quick technical checklist ahead of the deep-dive so we can use the 60 minutes effectively. Could you confirm the following items before the call or have answers ready:

1) Workload and performance
- Average tokens per request and worst-case tokens per request.
- Typical latency SLO (p50/p95) and any hard limits.
- Whether the 120 reqs/s peak is sustained or a short burst pattern.

2) Models and hosting
- Exact model names and any custom weights or fine-tuning.
- Which traffic you want routed to Redwood initially (all production, % split, or new features only).

3) Data and compliance
- Do you need message-level retention limits and KV cache eviction policies documented?
- Network requirements: IP allowlist, VPC peering, private endpoints, egress rules.

4) Auth and keys
- Key rotation policy and any existing secrets management you want to integrate (KMS/HSM).

Suggested migration approach (high level)
- Phase 1: Dual-write to Redwood Hosted API with prefix caching and request mirroring for live A/B and correctness checks.
- Phase 2: Dedicated pilot with autoscaling GPU pool to validate latency and cost; we can route a % of traffic from OpenAI to Redwood to compare.
- Phase 3: Private VPC data plane if needed for PHI and final cutover with a rollback window.

Ill bring a short migration runbook to the call that walks through required network changes and sample Terraform snippets. Link to runbook: https://redwood.ai/runbooks/migration-dual-write

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Tue 2026-06-30 14:00 PT, Wed 2026-07-01 15:00 PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
